hypothesis: If Darwin's claim holds, the numeric age of the end of the Secondary (Mesozoic) period, and of the latest Chalk, on the standard geological timescale is at least about 300 million years, since 'far more than 300 million years' are said to have elapsed since then.
pass_criterion: The ICS chart gives the top of the Cretaceous (end of the Chalk, the 'latter part of the Secondary period') an age of at least 270 Ma. That is within 10% of Darwin's 300 Myr or above it. The claim is also supported if the Campanian-Maastrichtian Chalk of the Weald dates to at least 270 Ma.
fail_criterion: The ICS chart gives the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary (end of the Secondary) an age below 150 Ma, i.e. less than half of Darwin's figure. The claim is also refuted if the youngest Chalk in the Weald dates below 150 Ma. The expected result is about 66 Ma, which would refute the claim by a factor of about 4.5.
interpretation: Darwin's 'Secondary period' is the Mesozoic. 'The latter part of the Secondary period' is the late Cretaceous, when the Chalk was deposited, ending at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary. His 306,662,400 years is a calculation from erosion of 1 inch per century on a 500-ft cliff, scaled to the Wealden denudation width. It is a prediction of elapsed time since the Chalk, so I test it against numeric radiometric and astrochronological ages on the ICS chart. The modern reinterpretation is that elapsed time since the Chalk is about 66-100 Myr, not more than 300 Myr. Darwin's erosion rate was used only as a proxy, so it is not tested separately.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart lists numeric boundary ages in Ma for every stage and system, and the landing page offers downloadable PDF, image and machine-readable versions. The fields used are the Cretaceous System upper boundary age (Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary) and the Upper Cretaceous stage boundary ages (Turonian to Maastrichtian), which cover the Chalk. These are compared with Darwin's approximately 300 Myr.
